reasoning: Both findings of the first round are answered by the simplest route: one conditioned stderr sentence, no report read, no helper, no SKILL.md rule, and the delta, tasks and map now say exactly that; reproduction, root cause, RED group and catcher hold.

simpler.evidence: design.md D1 now takes the simplest route — a fixed conditioned sentence appended to the incomplete-run message in skills/agent-process/scripts/check_red.py (tasks.md 2.1, one branch, no XML read, no helper) — and records the rejected alternative (trigger on a report `<error message="collection failure">`) with its cost: an XML read whose only gain is silence on a Ctrl-C, a usage error or an internal error, which the conditioned wording already covers, plus a tie to a junitxml attribute a pytest release could rename. D4 keeps it inside the existing gate. The delta carries no discriminator requirement and tasks.md no longer adds a negative assertion, so spec, design and tests describe one behaviour.

map.evidence: One delta scenario: `Test of code that does not exist yet` → tests/publisher/test_check_red.py::test_test_of_code_that_does_not_exist_yet (tasks.md map line 28, test name equal to the scenario name per that module's docstring); line 29 records `Configuration that cuts the run` as unchanged, matching the removal of the negative assertion. The scenario's `names the module that failed at collection` is proved through the pytest tail check_red already prints to stderr (design Context: `ERROR tests/test_greet.py`); in a pathological run the 4000-char `_TAIL_UNEVALUATED` cut could drop it, but the cut announces itself and names `--full` (check_red.py:_tail, §IV), so no scenario is left unprovable.

red.evidence: tasks.md 1.1 writes the live test (real pytest in tmp_path with its own quality declaration, parametrized over the node id at rc 4 and the file path at rc 2, asserting SystemExit 2 plus `test_greet` and `NotImplementedError` in stderr — the substring now matches pytest's own output rather than the dropped junit classname) and 1.2 runs `agent-process check_red tests/publisher/test_check_red.py::test_test_of_code_that_does_not_exist_yet`, expecting both parametrizations to fail on the stderr assertion, and commits RED before group 2. That RED is a body failure, not a collection error, because tests/publisher/test_check_red.py imports scripts through load_script inside each test, so check_red can judge it (error is not RED, check_red.py:evaluate_report).

platform.evidence: proposal.md Why records a live run of check_red's own command (pytest 9.0.3, Windows, this session): node ids give `ERROR: found no collectors`, `collected 0 items / 1 error`, rc=4; the file path gives `Interrupted: 1 error during collection`, rc=2. Those two rcs are the only platform facts the design now rests on — the report attribute is no longer read — and both are observed command output. The new Risks note on `--continue-on-collection-errors` is an accepted non-case with no code path: its in-repo half is verifiable (a report with `<error>` lands in the errored branch, check_red.py:150-159, which names the modules as not run), and its rc claim carries nothing.

replaced.evidence: No project-declared input is replaced and no guard dropped: exit 2 on an incomplete run, the unjudged report, `_COMPLETE_RUN`, `evaluate_report` and the existing message plus tail all stay (design Non-Goals; tasks.md 2.1 adds one stderr print and one docstring sentence). With the report read dropped there is not even a new input to fail.

catcher.evidence: design Risks names one catcher for the one risk that could silence the hint — a pytest release that ends an import error at collection as a complete run: the live test asserts SystemExit 2 on both spellings, so such a release makes it not-RED/exit 1 and the test red. Traced: tests/publisher/test_check_red.py::test_test_of_code_that_does_not_exist_yet runs under the declared `test` (.github/agent-process-quality.json → `python .agent-process/scripts/ci_check.py`, whose check_pytest runs `python -m pytest` over the repository tests, ci_check.py:273) in the `agent-process / quality` check on every PR head, including a Dependabot pytest-bump head; tasks.md 3.2 runs the same command on the delivery branch.

length.evidence: SKILL.md is untouched (proposal What Changes, design D2, no task 2.2), so no always-loaded rule prose is added and D2 records the trade it replaces — the gate's stderr reaches the same reader at the moment of failure, at the cost of one extra check_red call per change that tests new code, which is what issue #251's Brief asks for. The only added prose is the delta: a ~57-word requirement and a ~40-word scenario, whose load-bearing words the planned test asserts (exit 2, the module that failed at collection, the `NotImplementedError` stub, both selections); the trailing `so the test fails in its body` states what the hint conveys, not why the design was chosen.

bespoke.evidence: No script, check or helper is added: design D4 keeps the sentence inside the existing gate (issue #251) and names why no standard tool knows its boundary, and the pure helper of the previous round went with the report read, so no indirection with a single call site remains.
